plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double flowers atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed dark green foliage. A beloved cut flower and garden staple in temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in North America, Europe, and East Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live for more than 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on sugary nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely fragrant flowers and heart-shaped leaves. It thrives in cold-winter climates and is a hallmark of mid-spring gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (typically May in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; cultivated across Europe, North America, and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Lilac flowers are edible and have a floral, slightly bitter taste; they are used to flavor syrups, sugars, and baked goods.

plants.name: Rosa banksiae
plants.description: A vigorous, nearly thornless climbing rose that forms cascades of small, clustered, lightly violet-scented flowers. It is evergreen to semi-evergreen in warm climates and can cover entire buildings.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer (April to May, peaking around mid-May in many areas)
plants.location: Native to central and western China; naturalized in the southern United States and Mediterranean regions
plants.funFact: The largest rose plant in the world is a Lady Banks' rose in Tombstone, Arizona, planted in 1885, which covers over 8,000 square feet.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, fast-growing tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they fall. In the tropics and subtropics it blooms in the local spring; in parts of the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, such as Florida, Mexico, and southern California, it peaks around May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics; October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); cultivated in Mexico, the southern US, Africa, Australia, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas line the streets that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, and falling blossoms are said in folklore to bring good luck.
